pageTitle: Setting up AWS Firewall Manager policies
whatThePageStates: This is a one-paragraph section-landing (chapter index) page in the AWS WAF Developer Guide. Its entire body is a console-experience banner, a single sentence — "You can use AWS Firewall Manager to enable a number of different types of security policies. The steps for getting set up are slightly different for each." — followed by an auto-generated **Topics** list of eight links to child walkthrough pages, then the boilerplate "See also" AI-coding-assistant note. There is no table, no matrix, no Yes/No column, no availability wording, and no exclusion or "not supported" statement anywhere on the page. The page asserts only that setup procedures differ per policy type and points the reader at where each procedure lives; it makes no coverage claim about any axis, so features is empty.
shouldNotExtract: Everything on this page. Specifically: (1) the eight-item **Topics** list — this is AWS's standard auto-generated child-page navigation for a chapter node, identical in form to every other section index in the guide, and each entry is the title of a documentation page ("Setting up AWS Firewall Manager\u200b ... policies"), not a status cell; (2) the "Introducing a new console experience for AWS WAF" banner and its link to Working with the console; (3) the H1 and the anchor tag; (4) the "See also" block about Agent Toolkit skills and the aws agent-toolkit search-skills command, which is boilerplate appended to many pages in this guide; (5) the single lead sentence, which is prose framing ("a number of different types") and deliberately does not commit to a count.
coverageDimensions: REGION: nothing. The page never names a Region, an availability note, or an opt-in Region caveat. Any per-Region number attributed to this page is fabricated. SERVICE: nothing usable. Service names do appear inside the eight link titles (AWS WAF, AWS Shield Advanced, Amazon VPC, AWS Network Firewall, DNS Firewall, Palo Alto Networks Cloud NGFW, Fortigate CNF), but they appear as parts of documentation-page titles under a Topics heading, not as enumerated members of a supported-service list with any status attached. RESOURCE TYPE: nothing. No resource types, ARNs, or protected-resource kinds are named. The page also gives no counts, no tri-state values, and no scope dimension of any kind.
trap: The dominant trap is harvesting the eight **Topics** links as an eight-value coverage enumeration — most plausibly as policyType ("Firewall Manager supports 8 policy types") or as service/integrationType — and recording eight implicit Yes values. That is wrong twice over. First, the list is navigation: it enumerates child pages in the doc tree, and its membership tracks how the writers split the walkthroughs, not what Firewall Manager supports; the real Firewall Manager policy-type catalogue is published elsewhere and does not match this list one-for-one. Second, even read charitably it is a positives-only list with zero stated negatives, so it yields no denominator and no No count — absence of a policy type here is not a claim that it is unsupported. Runners-up: (a) treating the two third-party entries (Palo Alto Networks Cloud NGFW, Fortigate CNF) as evidence of a third-party-integration coverage matrix; (b) splitting the two Amazon VPC entries (security group, network ACL) into two service values, or collapsing them into one, both of which invent a granularity decision the page never makes; (c) mistaking the invisible zero-width space (U+200B) in "AWS Firewall Manager\u200b" for a delimiter and mis-tokenising the titles; (d) reading the console-experience banner or the "See also" Agent Toolkit paragraph as feature availability.
